content.theme: Today the theme was pressing, specifically focusing on the defenders' ability to identify a moment to press. The aim was for them to push into midfield, encouraging a midfielder to move onto the forward line, so the forwards could help defend or press the opposition's back line.
content.rhythm: Yes, the session flowed well between the introduction and the main part. Things were pretty smooth. We split between the two, first and reserves, then we came back together for a big game, and that worked pretty well.
content.nextTime: Next session, I'll try to come up with more cues for the players. They need to know what to look for before we jump and press.
content.wentWell: We had some moments in the main part where the defenders identified good moments to jump into midfield and push the midfielders on. That was good. There could have been more of those moments, but it was a bit easier to find the outcomes in a small-sided game during the intro.
content.learnings: I learned that I could have provided more solutions, even small ones, to give the players more cues. I probably didn't offer enough cues, and there needs to be more communication among the players in the moment.
content.challenges: The challenge today was the opposition. We wanted them to play in a way that allowed us to press, but they were building up quite fast. This didn't give our players much chance to identify a moment to jump.

content.theme: The theme of tonight's session was pressing, specifically getting the defenders to identify moments for a team press, pushing into midfield, and having the midfielders support the forwards to press the opponent's back line.
content.rhythm: The session flowed well between each part, from the intro or activation to the main part. Splitting into two teams worked well, and we came together nicely at the end for a big game.
content.nextTime: I'll come more prepared with cues for the main part. The activation was good, but I might make it a bit smaller to add more challenge.
content.wentWell: Some moments of success stood out with the defenders recognising when to push, and the midfielders following suit. There was good energy in the session, possibly due to the practices we set up or just a good vibe in the group tonight.
content.learnings: I need to think of more cues to help them press. While I gave them regular pressing cues, there could be other moments to press. I need to understand these cues better myself. When players were closely connected, pressing was easier. When spread out, they didn't try as they were too far apart.
content.challenges: The challenge was the opposition playing quickly, attacking rather than building up from the back. I struggled to find moments to press as they moved the ball upfield swiftly.

content.takeaways: We had a draw, and we're still five points clear. We need to focus on the next few games, avoid slipping on any banana peel matches, and get very focused for the Olympic game.
content.keyMoments: They brought two players on in the 57th minute, which was earlier than most coaches do. It gave us something to think about on the sidelines. It was nil all at the time, so we needed to rethink our subs or look at what he was doing with his team. Our number nine, DC, was a key moment. Irish, the centre-back, wasn't at his best today, maybe less composed than usual. They were closing us down quickly, so we'll need to think about separating the centre-backs more to prevent their number 9 from pressing us.
content.individuals: Izzy was her usual strong self. Rosie had a good game. Steffi didn't have her best game, missing a couple of sessions over the last two weeks hasn't helped her. Elena is a bit off her normal self after a big few weeks. DC is off at the moment, and that's okay. Lion is playing quite well.
content.improvements: We need to improve on taking our big chances and our one-on-one ability, as we missed two or three of those in the big game. Both full-backs played well. The goalkeeper needs to pick her moments to clear the ball forward and sometimes choose to kick it out sideways.
content.teamStrengths: Our shape was good. We didn't give away too many opportunities defensively. In attack, we were a bit disjointed, but we created the better chances throughout the day. Our forward play was stronger than theirs.

content.takeaways: Wanderers are struggling — no depth, no players of interest this year, no structure, very disorganised, too open. Only Adelaide can play for them. Keep an eye on Bronte's injury; keep building Isla's minutes.
content.keyMoments: The in-game press call — girls handled it well mid-game. Bronte going off injured early and Gemma settling after 10 minutes.
content.individuals: Bronte was injured — Gemma came in and played well after the first 10. Stefi was so good on the weak side defending, didn't need to be told at all. Isla going well with her minutes so far. Skelly starting to look red hot. Izzy still incredible, Ailish also, Leila playing well.
content.improvements: Not a lot to take from a game like this — they gave us too much space to really test us. Keep standards high when the opposition is struggling.
content.teamStrengths: We were far too good for them all over the park. Really pleased with the striker rotation — swapping the striker with Ailish worked nicely. Best bit: we did an in-game press and the girls executed it. Well done girls.

content.takeaways: Tuggies played a rough 5-3-2 — only interested in long ball, being direct, and trying not to lose by a lot. Purely set up to frustrate. For us: keep the tempo high, few touches, run forward off the ball.
content.keyMoments: Their whole game plan was to frustrate — our early passing and forward runs off the ball broke that open.
content.individuals: Girls playing quick tempo stood out. Leila good when she kept it sharp, dropped a level when she over-touched. Annie's first touch needs attention.
content.improvements: Tempo is the marker — when Leila took too many touches she came down a level. Annie's first touch is letting her down; something to work on this week.
content.teamStrengths: When we passed early, took only a few touches and ran off the ball forwards, it was impossible to track us. In general we were good — the girls who played at a quick tempo looked really good.

content.takeaways: Majura's 4-5-1 not very good. Manage Lily and Scarlett's minutes carefully; keep DC's scoring run going; factor in the synthetic surface for shooting and crossing sessions.
content.keyMoments: Elfin's debut going so well. Set pieces clicking through Izzy.
content.individuals: Leila in good form, and Bronte also. DC scoring goals which is good. Elfin's first game — really good. Izzy's set pieces good. Lily and Scarlett need more time before big minutes.
content.improvements: The synthetic made it hard to get good purchase on shots or crosses — worth noting for next time we're on it. Lily and Scarlett maybe not ready for lots of minutes yet and need some time.
content.teamStrengths: Comfortable all game. Izzy's set pieces were good, and DC scoring goals is a great sign.

content.takeaways: Olympic played a 4-3-3 and tried to rush us — big energy but no real quality. Tehya at CB is their one to watch. Our line-breaking possession is becoming a weapon; keep building it.
content.keyMoments: The 4-minute chat with the girls on the field at halftime — helped reset and confirmed some things Illya and I were seeing.
content.individuals: DC's goal quality again. Skelly building form and confidence — that dribble taking a couple of steps in to drag the defender one way, then going the other way around her. Tehya at CB is good for them.
content.improvements: Handling the atmosphere — their supporters are gross, too noisy and carry on. The on-field reset at halftime worked, so keep that tool handy for hostile away days.
content.teamStrengths: The girls played so well — the pass strings and the types of combinations were just so lethal. Not ineffective possession — killer possession. Real quality breaking lines and leaving them clueless.

content.theme: Today's theme was around pressing and finding ways to identify when to press during the game moment, as opposed to just in goal kicks. We talked about cues or triggers that might help us make the call to press.
content.rhythm: The session flowed well between each part, but the passing activation wasn't ideal because I didn't have the cones, and the length of the pass wasn't far enough.
content.nextTime: I've changed the length of the passing practice. It was too short on the sides.
content.wentWell: We trained 11 v 11 because we didn't have enough players to split into two. This allowed for more realism as it was like a game. We could set the team up to look for real moments, unlike the 6 v 7 we initially planned.
content.learnings: I learned that the players appreciated having an assistant coach manage the team that is not being coached. We usually don't focus on managing the other team, but we're making a conscious decision to start doing that.
content.challenges: The technical activation was challenging because I didn't have similar things to talk about that matched up with the main part. The coaching or learning points weren't really connected, which was difficult.

content.theme: The theme was being patient when we're building up from the back, or just in general when we're building up by trying to rush.
content.rhythm: Yes, the session had good flow between it today. The energy was high, big time we moved to the next one.
content.nextTime: I don't think anything. It was just a good session. Really good session. Probably the best rehearsal of all.
content.wentWell: All three parts, the passing activation, there was a lot of energy, they enjoyed the different movements and combinations. The activation had good energy, they really enjoyed the practice when it was 10 players because it was a bit more dynamic, the 12 players was a bit more stationary, a bit less real, so the feedback for that would be that. And the main part just had a lot of energy. The seven and eight a side in that setup is a lot smoother than 11 and 11.
content.learnings: I think we had the week off last week, and they just had a lot of energy. I think they just ready to play again.
content.challenges: The numbers were challenging tonight, 21, 22 is a difficult number, it was more like 23, so too much for 11 a side, and not enough for two full separate training groups.
